title: I got Tekken 8 gameplay running in a web engine, directly in the browser
author: Emulator000
selftext:
After my Tekken 3 experiment in DriftEngine, I decided to try something much more ambitious: Tekken 8.

I now have an actual Kazuya vs Jin fight running, which also means it can run directly inside a modern web browser through WebGPU.

This is not cloud streaming, emulation or Unreal Engine running somewhere in the background.

The demo already has the loading screen, character intros, full HUD, moves and throws, Heat mechanics, win/lose logic, screen effects, character VFX, confetti and a fully rendered stage with its dynamic effects.

So this has gone quite a bit beyond simply loading models and animations, DriftEngine reads the assets from my own legitimately purchased Tekken 8 installation and handles the runtime, rendering, animation, gameplay and VFX through a completely different engine.

For me, the browser part makes this especially interesting because DriftEngine is primarily a TypeScript/WebGPU engine, so getting this far with a modern AAA game is a pretty extreme test of what the architecture can handle.

There is still a lot missing and plenty to improve, but honestly I didn't expect to get this far this quickly.

DriftEngine:  
[https://driftengine.dev/](https://driftengine.dev/)

GitHub:  
[https://github.com/drftrun/driftengine](https://github.com/drftrun/driftengine)

This is currently a private technical experiment. I'm not distributing Tekken 8, its assets or its game files.
